title: Sitting down to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma…
content: Sitting down to one side, the Venerable Rādha said to the Blessed One: “Good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief. Having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I will dwell alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute.” - “Rādha, whatever is impermanent — there you should abandon your desire. And what, Rādha, is impermanent? The eye, Rādha, is impermanent — there you should abandon your desire. Forms are impermanent … Eye-consciousness … Eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact — pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that feeling is impermanent. There you should abandon your desire. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … The mind is impermanent — there you should abandon your desire. Phenomena … Mind-consciousness … Mind-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact — pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that feeling is impermanent. There you should abandon your desire. Whatever is impermanent, Rādha — there you should abandon your desire.”

title: “Monks, one who dwells seeing danger in things that are fetters — greed is abandoned, hatred is abandoned, delusion is abandoned. Because greed, hatred, and…
content: “Monks, one who dwells seeing danger in things that are fetters — greed is abandoned, hatred is abandoned, delusion is abandoned. Because greed, hatred, and delusion are abandoned, he is freed from birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is freed from suffering.”

title: “Once, monks, a hawk suddenly swooped down and seized a quail. Then, monks, the quail, while being carried off by the hawk, lamented: ‘This is…
content: “Once, monks, a hawk suddenly swooped down and seized a quail. Then, monks, the quail, while being carried off by the hawk, lamented: ‘This is my misfortune! This is my lack of merit! For I wandered outside my own proper range, into the domain of others. If I had kept to my own proper range, my ancestral territory, this hawk would not have been a match for me in battle.’ - ‘What, quail, is your own proper range, your ancestral territory?’ - ‘A field plowed with a plow.’ Then, monks, the hawk, not boasting of its own strength, not pressing its own strength, released the quail and said: ‘Go, quail. Even after going there, I will not let you go.’ Then, monks, the quail went to a field plowed with a plow, climbed onto a large clod of earth, stood on it, and said to the hawk: ‘Come at me, hawk! Come at me, hawk!’ Then the hawk, boasting of its own strength, pressing its own strength, folding both wings, suddenly swooped down on the quail. When the quail knew: ‘This hawk is swooping down hard on me,’ it hid behind that clod of earth. Then, monks, the hawk shattered its own breast. So too, monks, for one who wanders outside his own proper range, into the domain of others. Therefore, monks, do not wander outside your own proper range, into the domain of others. For one who wanders outside his proper range, into the domain of others, Māra gains an opportunity, Māra gains an object.”

title: “Monks, there is no form that is permanent, everlasting, eternal, not subject to change, that will remain forever. There is no feeling … perception ……
content: “Monks, there is no form that is permanent, everlasting, eternal, not subject to change, that will remain forever. There is no feeling … perception … formation … consciousness that is permanent, everlasting, eternal, not subject to change, that will remain forever.”

title: “Monks, just as a great tree, having its roots that extend downward and laterally, all those roots convey the sap upwards — that great tree,…
content: “Monks, just as a great tree, having its roots that extend downward and laterally, all those roots convey the sap upwards — that great tree, being nourished and sustained in such a way, would stand for a long time. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are clung to — craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging arises … Thus the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Monks, just as a great tree, and a man comes with a shovel and a basket. He cuts the tree’s roots … He digs a trench … he pulls out the rootlets … or he burns the tree and scatters the ashes in a strong stream of water. That great tree, with its roots cut, made like a palm stump, cannot be reborn, cannot arise again in the future. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing peril in things that are clung to — craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases … Thus the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: “Monks, if a monk, while attending to some sign and giving attention to it, has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arise.…
content: “Monks, if a monk, while attending to some sign and giving attention to it, has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arise. That monk attends to a different sign connected with what is wholesome, not that sign. Those evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion are abandoned and subside. With their abandonment, the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”

title: “And how, monks, is a monk ‘one who has learned’? He has destroyed evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing…
content: “And how, monks, is a monk ‘one who has learned’? He has destroyed evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is ‘one who has learned.’”

title: “Sāriputta, while a noble disciple attains and dwells in the rapture born of seclusion, during that time five things do not occur for him: pain…
content: “Sāriputta, while a noble disciple attains and dwells in the rapture born of seclusion, during that time five things do not occur for him: pain and grief connected with sensuality do not occur; pleasure and joy connected with sensuality do not occur; pain and grief connected with the unwholesome do not occur; pleasure and joy connected with the unwholesome do not occur; pain and grief connected with the wholesome do not occur. Sāriputta, while a noble disciple attains and dwells in the rapture born of seclusion, during that time these five things do not occur for him.”

title: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
content: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, there is an establishment of consciousness. When consciousness is established and grows, there is the descent of name-and-form. With name-and-form as condition, the six sense-bases; with the six sense-bases as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling … craving … clinging … existence … birth; aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk does not delight in…
content: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk does not delight in those forms, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them — then that monk is called one who has not swallowed Māra’s hook, who has broken the hook, destroyed the hook, who has not fallen into misfortune, into calamity, not subject to the Evil One’s will. There are sounds … odors … tastes … touches … phenomena cognizable by the mind … If a monk does not delight in those phenomena, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them — then that monk is called one who has not swallowed Māra’s hook, who has broken the hook, destroyed the hook, who has not fallen into misfortune, into calamity, not subject to the Evil One’s will.”
